messages.author: Piia Bartos
messages.body:
Hi,
Amber deals with different molecules (protein, RNA, DNA, small molecules..) in different force fields. How are the interfaces between different force fields dealt with? Could you point me to some literature about this?
Cheers,
Piia Bartos

messages.author: Piia Bartos
messages.body:
Yes, I am thinking about these kind of interactions:
Lets assume there is an O atom in DNA and in a protein. When counting the non-bonded interaction between these atoms, the partial charges and LJ radius are needed. Are these parameters taken from the DNA force field or from the protein force field? Or are the parameters mixed so that each atom takes them from their own force field?
Cheers,
Piia

messages.author: Carlos Simmerling
messages.body:
They are mixed. You do need to be careful about combining for fields, but
most of the ones included in Amber are designed to be mixed like this.
There is a good description at
http://ambermd.org/AmberModels.php

messages.author: Maria Nagan
messages.body:
I would look at the literature listed for each force field. You need a different force field for each biomolecules/type of entity in the simulation. Some go better with others. Look at each paper and the recommendations on the force field pages.
Maria
